positions.name: CalibrationGroundedInReferenceVerification
positions.frame: does the calibration's validity rest on verification against a fixed external reference standard, or on the instrument reading alone?
positions.why: Both expressions ground the calibration claim in the same specific act — verification against the June reference plates — rather than in the instrument reading standing alone. src-1 performs this in flat confident prose ('verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it holds across the full observing band'); src-3 compresses the same claim into a spec-line register ('88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates'). The directional observations reinforce the read: both carry authority-ranking (the reference plates arbitrate the instrument's output) and a competence value (validated craft), with matching claim-level conviction and calm-positive, technical-matter-of-fact delivery. No tension between the two — the bullet is a compressed restatement of the prose's verification claim, not a competing one.
